status: SEARCH HEURISTIC FOR LOCATION, NOT A MATHEMATICAL CLAIM
disclaimer: This file tags declarations with the REGION OF THE NUMBER LINE their
quantified variable ranges over, relative to the square-root scale.
A region tag is evidence that a declaration's statement text contains a
particular cut, nothing more. Two declarations sharing a region tag are a
reason to read both. They are NOT thereby about the same object, on the
same carrier, or at the same scale, and AGENTS.md rule 5 still applies in
full: never infer that two quantities are equal because their regions,
names or prose descriptions line up. Use or prove an exact bridge theorem.
Evidence is reported in two strictly separated grades:
direct  -- an actual index range or inequality in the statement text,
anchored to a variable the same statement pins to the
square-root scale. This is the grade worth trusting.
lexical -- a declaration or module name token. A naming convention, and
names in this repository have been wrong before. Never used
to place a declaration on its own in any report that claims
coverage; always shown as the weaker grade it is.
Coverage is deliberately low. Most declarations are helper lemmas that
carry no cut of their own and inherit their region from a caller. The
layer does not guess for them; an untagged declaration is reported as
untagged rather than assigned a plausible region.

note: The library's square-root scale variable is written R (also W, X, N).
The span is x = R^2 - 1, so R is exactly the square root of x + 1.
Both identities below are definitional in compiled source, which is why
the two spellings may be normalised onto each other. This is a read
identity, not an inference from similar names.

identities.lean: RoughAbove b m = forall p in m.primeFactors, b < p

axes.span: Where the running variable sits on [1, x] relative to the root scale R.
axes.factor: Where the PRIME FACTORS sit. A different geometry from span: a large integer may be rough, a small one smooth. Never conflated with a span region.

below-root.description: The square-prefix / low-cofactor region. Work that stays strictly below the square-root scale.

above-root.description: The post-root region: everything strictly above the square-root scale, with no finer cut stated.

mid-band.description: The middle band: above the square root, at or below half the span. Strictly inside above-root.

top-fibre.description: The top fibre: primes above half the span, where floor(x/q) = 1 so the only surviving cofactor is c = 1. Strictly inside above-root.

full-span.description: The whole range to the stated cutoff, with no interior cut. Scale-aware but not located: it does not distinguish either side of the square root.

square-block.description: One square annulus between consecutive square-prefix endpoints. Indexed by block number, so it is not comparable to the root-relative regions without naming the block.

rough-above.cut: every prime factor of m exceeds b
rough-above.description: Roughness: the small primes have been sieved out. A constraint on prime factors, not on magnitude.

wheel-coprime.cut: coprime to a primorial wheel W
wheel-coprime.description: The wheel-coprime population: the smooth part below the wheel has been removed. Also a prime-factor constraint.

containment.why: (R, x/2] is a subset of (R, x] whenever x/2 <= x.
(x/2, x] is a subset of (R, x] whenever R <= x/2.
[1, R) is a subset of [1, x] whenever R <= x.
(R, x] is a subset of [1, x].

partitions.why: Ioc R x = Ioc R (x/2) union Ioc (x/2) x, disjointly, for R <= x/2.

provenance: Region ids, cuts and detection patterns were derived by enumerating every
Finset range and scale comparison that actually occurs in RHLean/**/*.lean,
not by proposing a vocabulary and looking for matches. Rebuild the census
with `python3 scripts/region_graph.py --census` after the library grows.
